spans.claim: The body was found with a deep gash in his throat and a razor in his hand
spans.anchor: a deep gash in his throat, in his stiffened hand a razor
spans.span: In a small dressing-room, leading off the bedroom which fronted the square, they found a gruesome sight--the lifeless body of a man, comparatively young, somewhere about thirty-five or so, a deep gash in his throat, in his stiffened hand a razor.

spans.claim: Letters addressed to Reginald Davis were found on the dead man
spans.anchor: three letters addressed to Reginald Davis
spans.span: On the body of the dead man in Cathcart Square, the two constables had found three letters addressed to Reginald Davis.

spans.claim: Caroline Masters identified the body as her brother Reginald Davis
spans.anchor: identified the body as that of her brother, Reginald Davis
spans.span: A tall, handsome young woman, giving the name of Caroline Masters, had been to the mortuary, and identified the body as that of her brother, Reginald Davis.

spans.claim: Norah Burton is also known as Stella Keane and Mrs Spencer
spans.anchor: Norah Burton (also Stella Keane, Mrs Spencer)

spans.claim: George Burton is also known as George Dutton, a criminal forger
spans.anchor: George Burton (also George Dutton)

spans.claim: Major Hugh Murchison was murdered and his body buried as Reginald Davis
spans.anchor: the exhumed body was found to be that of Major Murchison
spans.span: The exhumed body was found to be that of Major Murchison, wrongly identified in the first instance as that of Reginald Davis.

spans.claim: The murderers forged a letter from Reginald Davis to the Coroner
spans.anchor: a letter, signed Reginald Davis, addressed to the Coroner
spans.span: Also a letter, signed Reginald Davis, addressed to the Coroner in which he avowed his intention of committing suicide at the earliest opportunity.

spans.claim: The diary of Major Murchison revealed the truth about the murder
spans.anchor: a diary, bound in red leather, a small volume
spans.span: But they did find one priceless thing, and that was a diary, bound in red leather, a small volume as to the size of the page, but very bulky.

spans.claim: Mrs Spencer was identified by Scotland Yard detective Bryant as Norah Burton
spans.anchor: Bryant would swear to the identification
spans.span: Bryant would swear to the identification, and Parkinson would swear that Mrs Guy Spencer, once Norah Burton, had met George Burton clandestinely four times in a fortnight, and had supplied him with money.

spans.claim: Mrs Spencer and George Dutton met clandestinely and exchanged money
spans.anchor: Mrs Spencer slip an envelope into his hand
spans.span: For on the last two occasions when I followed them in, and sat at a table where I could observe them, I saw Mrs Spencer slip an envelope into his hand.

spans.claim: Norah Burton and George Burton committed suicide to avoid arrest
spans.anchor: Norah Burton, and the man who had been so long associated with her... had gone to their judgment

spans.claim: Reginald Davis was alive and hiding under an assumed name
spans.anchor: The late Reginald Davis, very alive and well
spans.span: The late Reginald Davis, very alive and well, knocked at the door of his sister's flat.

spans.claim: Caroline Masters falsely identified the dead man to protect her brother
spans.anchor: she swore it was you, and gave you a new lease of life

spans.claim: Iris Deane had an alibi during the murder
spans.anchor: I motored down to Brighton with Johnny Lascelles
spans.span: I motored down to Brighton with Johnny Lascelles--who, by the way, used to make Roddie fearfully jealous.

spans.claim: The broken window was used to gain entry to the house
spans.anchor: somebody had smashed the pane in order to get at the latch
spans.span: That somebody had smashed the pane in order to get at the latch, had entered the house, later emerged through the window and forgotten to fasten it.

spans.claim: Caretaker Miles was absent during the murder and had an alibi
spans.anchor: The bed was empty. Miles had evidently taken a holiday
spans.span: The bed was empty. Miles had evidently taken a holiday.

spans.claim: Jack Pomfret married Norah Burton secretly and committed suicide
spans.anchor: Jack Pomfret... had made the girl his wife a few hours previously

spans.span: Bryant would swear to the identification, and Parkinson would swear that Mrs Guy Spencer, once Norah Burton, had met George Burton clandestinely four times in a fortnight, and had supplied him with money.

spans.claim: The diary contained a confession and plan to expose Norah Burton
spans.anchor: I have drawn up two copies of the confession, one of which she is to sign

spans.claim: The murder was committed by drugging and cutting the victim's throat
spans.anchor: she had sprayed over him the essence of some overpowering and stupefying drug
spans.span: While talking to him, she had sprayed over him the essence of some overpowering and stupefying drug, and while he was staggering about, dazed and blinded, the man had stepped in and done the rest.
